staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `737a853f8db69fb09a51351d3b505d008b03bbb3`, but the line anchors below are resolved against the staged tree that still contains the vulnerable code and matches the saved crash.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42490511 (glib): Global-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzz_date_time_new_from_iso8601 [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42490511
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 327-byte ASCII string in `poc` beginning `0004157 200007.` and ending `5007-02` (sha256 `d07acbf090041ca45227e0cff5e255b557eb45c8e884345ef99e8f8bc6180c34`). `g_date_time_new_from_iso8601()` finds the space separator, accepts the `-02` timezone suffix, parses the date as ordinal `YYYYDDD` (`year = 4`, `ordinal_day = 157`), and routes the `07.<309-digit>` seconds field into `get_iso8601_seconds()`. That helper accumulates both the numerator and divisor in `gdouble`; with 309 fractional digits both leave finite range and the final `v / divisor` becomes a non-finite `seconds` value (`NaN` on the crashing path). Vulnerable `g_date_time_new()` checks only `seconds < 0.0 || seconds >= 60.0`, so it accepts the non-finite value, feeds it into integer-based time calculations, and writes invalid `datetime->days` / `datetime->usec` state instead of returning `NULL`. `g_date_time_new_ordinal()` then adds the ordinal-day offset to that corrupted day count, and the fuzzer formats the returned object with `g_date_time_format_iso8601()`. In the `%Y` formatter path, `g_date_time_get_ymd()` derives an out-of-range month estimate and executes `days_in_year[0][the_month - 1]`, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` 14 bytes to the left of global `days_in_year`. The fix closes both ends of this chain by rejecting non-finite parsed seconds in `get_iso8601_seconds()` and adding `!isfinite (seconds)` to `g_date_time_new()`.

source.description: First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled long fractional-seconds substring into the parser's `seconds` output.
source.value_from: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_42490511/poc` (327 ASCII bytes, sha256 `d07acbf090041ca45227e0cff5e255b557eb45c8e884345ef99e8f8bc6180c34`): ordinal date `0004157`, a space separator, time prefix `200007.`, a 309-digit fractional seconds field, and timezone suffix `-02`. Harness line `fuzzing/fuzz_date_time_new_from_iso8601.c:12-13` NUL-terminates that string with `g_strndup()` and passes it to `g_date_time_new_from_iso8601()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.code:
if (year < 1 || year > 9999 ||
    month < 1 || month > 12 ||
    day < 1 || day > days_in_months[GREGORIAN_LEAP (year)][month] ||
    hour < 0 || hour > 23 ||
    minute < 0 || minute > 59 ||
    seconds < 0.0 || seconds >= 60.0)
  return NULL;
root_cause.description: Root cause. `g_date_time_new()` validates the numeric range of `seconds` but omits the missing `!isfinite (seconds)` obligation, so a non-finite value bypasses the constructor precondition.
root_cause.note: For the witness's non-finite `seconds`, both `seconds < 0.0` and `seconds >= 60.0` evaluate false, so the constructor continues into integer-based time calculations instead of rejecting the input. The fix adds `!isfinite (seconds)` here and also hardens `get_iso8601_seconds()`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `g_date_time_get_ymd()` uses the corrupted month estimate to index before the static `days_in_year` table while formatting the returned `GDateTime`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 2` at `glib/gdatetime.c:2188:16` and says the faulting address is 14 bytes to the left of global `days_in_year` defined at `glib/gdatetime.c:175`. Since `days_in_year[0]` is a 13-entry `guint16` row, that offset corresponds to indexing 7 elements before `days_in_year[0][0]`, i.e. `the_month - 1 == -7` on the crashing execution.

tainted_value_origin.description: The non-finite `seconds` value originates here. After the witness's `07.<309 fractional digits>` tail is accumulated in floating `v` / `divisor` accumulators, the final division writes that non-finite result back through `value` to the caller's `seconds` variable.

parser_admitted.description: The witness contains a space date/time separator and a `-02` timezone suffix, so `g_date_time_new_from_iso8601()` enters time parsing on `200007.<309 fractional digits>-02`. `parse_iso8601_time()` recognizes the `hhmmss(.sss)` form, strips the timezone into a non-NULL `tz`, and routes the `07.<309 digits>` substring into `get_iso8601_seconds()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `parse_iso8601_time()` has already stripped the `-02` suffix and selected the `hhmmss(.sss)` branch for the witness tail `200007.<309 digits>`. By the time this division executes, the 309 fractional digits have driven both `v` and `divisor` beyond finite `gdouble` range, so `*value` becomes a non-finite `seconds` result (`NaN` on the crashing path).

fine_trace.code: return g_date_time_new_ordinal (tz, year, ordinal_day, hour, minute, seconds);
fine_trace.note: The date prefix `0004157` takes the `YYYYDDD` branch, yielding `year == 4` and `ordinal_day == 157`. Because the same parse also produced a non-NULL timezone from suffix `-02`, this call forwards the non-finite `seconds` from step 1 into `g_date_time_new_ordinal()` instead of returning `NULL`.

fine_trace.code:
if (year < 1 || year > 9999 ||
    month < 1 || month > 12 ||
    day < 1 || day > days_in_months[GREGORIAN_LEAP (year)][month] ||
    hour < 0 || hour > 23 ||
    minute < 0 || minute > 59 ||
    seconds < 0.0 || seconds >= 60.0)
  return NULL;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The constructor checks only the numeric range of `seconds`. For the non-finite value from step 1, both comparisons at the end of this guard are false, so the function accepts the input and continues instead of rejecting it. The fix adds `!isfinite (seconds)` here.

fine_trace.code:
full_time = SEC_PER_DAY *
              (ymd_to_days (year, month, day) - UNIX_EPOCH_START) +
            SECS_PER_HOUR * hour +
            SECS_PER_MINUTE * minute +
            (int) seconds;

datetime->interval = g_time_zone_adjust_time (datetime->tz,
                                              G_TIME_TYPE_STANDARD,
                                              &full_time);
fine_trace.note: With step 3's guard bypassed, the constructor feeds the non-finite `seconds` into the whole-second timestamp via `(int) seconds` and then passes that timestamp through `g_time_zone_adjust_time()` using the parsed `-02` timezone. This creates a non-finite-derived `full_time` that step 5 later stores back into the object as calendar state.

The constructor next derives the microsecond remainder from the same non-finite `seconds` and overwrites `datetime->days` and `datetime->usec` from `full_time` and `usec`. The staged artifacts do not expose the exact intermediate integers, but the later sink proves this stored `datetime->days` is no longer a valid Gregorian day count.

The ordinal-date wrapper then adds `ordinal_day - 1 == 156` to the already-invalid day count returned by steps 3-5 so the object represents date `0004-157` rather than January 1. This mutated `dt->days` is the state later consumed by the formatter.

The fuzz target formats any non-NULL result with `g_date_time_format_iso8601()`, whose fixed format string begins with `%Y`. This `%Y` case therefore asks `g_date_time_get_year(datetime)` for the year and forces `g_date_time_get_ymd()` to interpret the corrupted day count from step 6.

Inside `g_date_time_get_ymd()`, `remaining_days` was initialized from `datetime->days` and reduced through the 400/100/4/1-year cycle math before this month estimate. On the crashing execution that estimate left the valid `1..12` range; the ASan offset at the next line implies `the_month - 1 == -7`, i.e. `the_month == -6`.

Sink. `days_in_year[0]` is a 13-entry `guint16` row indexed validly only by `0..12`, but step 8 produced `the_month - 1 == -7`. This 2-byte read therefore lands 14 bytes before global `days_in_year`, exactly matching the saved `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `glib/gdatetime.c:2188`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the exact top project frame in the saved ASan trace: `g_date_time_get_ymd()` at `glib/gdatetime.c:2188`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable. This is a global-buffer-overflow on the static table `days_in_year`, not a heap allocation or lifetime bug.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `g_date_time_get_ymd -> g_date_time_get_year -> g_date_time_format_utf8 -> g_date_time_format -> g_date_time_format_iso8601 -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the tail of the fine trace exactly; the earlier parser and constructor steps are the source-side logic that occurs before the saved crash stack begins.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness's 309-digit fractional seconds field becomes non-finite in step 1, bypasses the step-3 constructor guard, is stored into corrupted `datetime->days` state in steps 4-6, and reaches the step-9 out-of-bounds `days_in_year` read through the `%Y` formatter path.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42490511 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow`, `READ of size 2`, and the stack `g_date_time_get_ymd -> g_date_time_get_year -> g_date_time_format_utf8 -> g_date_time_format -> g_date_time_format_iso8601 -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: raw ISO-8601 ordinal-date witness string
format.contract: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_42490511/poc` (327 ASCII bytes, sha256 `d07acbf090041ca45227e0cff5e255b557eb45c8e884345ef99e8f8bc6180c34`): a single ISO-8601 string with ordinal date `0004157`, a space separator, time prefix `200007.`, a 309-digit fractional-seconds field, and timezone suffix `-02`. The staged artifacts prove that this exact long-fraction witness can make `get_iso8601_seconds()` produce a non-finite `seconds` value and reach the saved crash; they do not establish a broader trigger contract beyond this witness.
